title: ACR Helper: a Google Meet™ add-on for a committee deciding on one applicant at a time
body: This video shows the whole workflow end to end, on a spreadsheet of made-up applicants labeled TEST.
Scopes requested: openid, userinfo.email, userinfo.profile, and spreadsheets. Nothing else is read from Google, and no spreadsheet data is sent to any server.

kicker: 1 · Sign in inside Meet's side panel
title: Google's One Tap prompt, then Google's consent screen
body: openid, userinfo.email, userinfo.profile: the panel signs the person in with Google One Tap and shows their name to the committee when they vote.
spreadsheets: asked for next, in Google's own window, so the add-on can open the committee's spreadsheet as that person.

title: The panel opens the committee's spreadsheet with the person's own token
body: It checks that this person can open the spreadsheet; someone who cannot sees only a refusal.
Start review reads the first row without a decision and shows that applicant on Meet's main stage.

title: Private votes, revealed together
body: Each member votes in their own panel; no one sees a choice until the chair presses Reveal.

title: The chair records the decision; a note is added
body: Record writes the committee's decision into that applicant's row, with a cell note naming who recorded it and when.
Add note appends a line to the row's Notes from Admissions cell. Nothing else in the spreadsheet is changed.

title: What ACR Helper wrote
body: The decision cell (Maybe = Waitlist) and its note, the appended line in Notes from Admissions, and a hidden tab holding the key that encrypts messages between members' add-ons.

title: One spreadsheet, the person's own permission, nothing kept elsewhere
list: openid, userinfo.email, userinfo.profile: sign-in, and the voter's name
spreadsheets: read the committee's spreadsheet; write the decision, a note, and the hidden key tab
No other spreadsheet, file, or Google data is opened
